The [Electoral College](/wiki/United_States_Electoral_College "United States Electoral College"), every four years, elects the [President](/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") and [Vice President of the United States](/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States "Vice President of the United States") based on the popular vote in each state and the District of Columbia. Each state's number of votes in the Electoral College is equal to its number of members in the Senate plus members in the House of Representatives.[[5]](#cite_note-auto-5)

The [Twenty-third Amendment to the United States Constitution](/wiki/Twenty-third_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Twenty-third Amendment to the United States Constitution") additionally grants the District of Columbia (D.C.), which is not a state, as many Electoral College votes as it would have if it *were* a state, while having no more votes than the least populous state (Wyoming). Since the U.S. Constitution guarantees every state at least one member of the U.S. House of Representatives and two members of the U.S. Senate, every state has at least three Electoral College votes. Thus, the Electoral College has 538 members (100 [senators](/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"), plus 435 representatives due to the limit imposed by the Reapportionment Act of 1929, plus 3 members for the District of Columbia).[[5]](#cite_note-auto-5) [Territories of the United States](/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States "Territories of the United States") are not included in the Electoral College: people in those territories cannot vote directly for the President of the United States,[[6]](#cite_note-6) although they may participate in the partisan nominating primaries and caucuses.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

Officially, the vice premiers are appointed by the [National People's Congress](/wiki/National_People%27s_Congress "National People's Congress") (NPC) upon the nomination of the premier.[[4]](#cite_note-:023-4) The NPC also has the power to remove the vice premiers and other state officers from office. Elections and removals are decided by majority vote.[[4]](#cite_note-:023-4) In practice, the vice premiers are chosen within the [Chinese Communist Party](/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") (CCP) leadership, including the Politburo Standing Committee.[[5]](#cite_note-:82-5) Candidates for top positions including the vice premier are first approved first by the CCP's Politburo Standing Committee, and then by its [Politburo](/wiki/Politburo_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "Politburo of the Chinese Communist Party"), then approved in a special plenary session the Central Committee just before the NPC session for vote by the Congress, with the premier nominating the candidates during the NPC session.[[6]](#cite_note-:822-6)

The length of the vice premier's term of office is the same as the NPC, which is 5 years, and the vice premiers are restricted to two consecutive terms.[[4]](#cite_note-:023-4) Immediately after the election, the [president](/wiki/President_of_China "President of China") signs the presidential order formalizing the appointment of the vice premiers. Since 2018, the vice premiers are required to collectively [recite](/wiki/Recitation "Recitation") the [constitutional oath of office](/wiki/Constitutional_oath_of_office_of_China "Constitutional oath of office of China") before assuming office.[[5]](#cite_note-:82-5)
